findings.quote: 後唐清泰三年二月，原州刺史翟建奏
findings.reason: The date precedes the named subject and verb: Zhai Jian, prefect of Yuan, memorialized in Qingtai 3, second lunar month. The following first-person memorial requests the transfer of Linjing from Jing's jurisdiction; 從之 closes this administrative entry. This securely attests the named official's activity at the time of the memorial.

findings.quote: 本州自陷吐蕃，權於臨涇縣為理所
findings.reason: 自陷 introduces prior background to the current petition, not a new conquest in Qingtai 3. Nothing dates Zhai Jian's birth, appointment, start of service, or participation in that earlier conquest. The county's administrative arrangement is not a lifetime interval for him.

findings.quote: 後唐清泰三年正月，涇州奏
findings.reason: The preceding Pingliang entry has its own first-month date, petitioner Jing prefecture, and closing 從之. The Linjing heading begins a separate paragraph, whose explicit second-month date overrides any attempted inheritance of the previous date. The following Fucheng entry is separately dated to Liang Kaiping and Later Tang Tongguang. None of these dates belongs to Zhai Jian.

findings.quote: 清泰三年春正月辛卯朔
findings.reason: Jiu Wudai Shi 48 independently supplies the Qingtai 3 annalistic frame and Xinmao first day of month one. Academia Sinica's Later Tang / Feidi / Qingtai 3 conversion returns the same Xinmao new-year day and an ordinary second month wholly in AD 936. Its second-month first and thirtieth days are Julian 936-02-25 and 936-03-25; the next month begins Julian 936-03-26. These are calendar boundary queries, never asserted memorial dates. At year-only precision the Gregorian year is also 936; a February/March Julian span cannot cross a Gregorian year boundary. No Gregorian month/day or interval is proposed.

findings.quote: 天福元年（丙申，公元九三六年）
findings.reason: The modern transcription of Tongjian 280 labels this annual sequence Tianfu 1 / bingshen / AD 936 and records Tang's elevation of Chongmei in the first month and Ma Yinsun's appointment in the third, matching the sequence in Jiu Wudai Shi 48 under Qingtai 3. The AD numeral is modern editorial apparatus, not original Song text; it is corroboration only. This source does not independently attest Zhai Jian or supply a day for his memorial. Later Jin's annual heading must not change the petition's explicit Later Tang polity.

Maxwell correctly acknowledged the explicit source date, but deferred conversion because the earlier editorial review lacked authorization for chronology. That was a workflow boundary, not source ambiguity. The new narrow authorization and independently checked calendar support replacing both unresolved fields and the research-required hint. Merely retaining an unnecessary unresolved reason would conceal readily resolvable date capture. Unknown day remains unasserted, not converted to a first-of-month event date. Year-only precision is deliberate lossless preservation of certainty when the exact lunar expression remains in sourceDate.text.

The reviewed 176 source repairs alter English fields only. In this paragraph, s0124-s0126 retain both English fields exactly; s0127 only changes note-closing punctuation. All 234 Chinese units, their order, and locators remain exact. A changed source file hash from those reviewed English repairs requires normal packet/evidence reconciliation but is not contrary chronology evidence.
